title: Blood Pressure Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Blood Pressure Calculator](/blood-pressure-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Classify an adult blood-pressure reading and calculate pulse pressure and mean arterial pressure. Enter your systolic pressure (top number) and diastolic pressure (bottom number) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Blood pressure is recorded as systolic over diastolic pressure in millimetres of mercury. This adult screening tool assigns the entered reading to categories based on common US ACC/AHA thresholds and calculates two derived values: pulse pressure and estimated mean arterial pressure. It does not diagnose hypertension, which normally requires repeated correctly measured readings on different days and clinical interpretation. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Blood Pressure Calculator

Start by entering your systolic pressure (top number) (mmHg), then entering your diastolic pressure (bottom number) (mmHg). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Sit quietly for at least five minutes, with your back supported, feet flat and arm supported at heart level.
2. Use a validated, correctly fitting cuff and take readings without talking; repeat as advised and average consistent results.
3. Enter the top systolic and bottom diastolic numbers, then discuss persistently abnormal readings with a qualified clinician.

## Formula

Pulse pressure = systolic − diastolic. Estimated mean arterial pressure = (systolic + 2 × diastolic) ÷ 3, reflecting the longer diastolic portion of a typical cardiac cycle.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Blood Pressure Calculator](/blood-pressure-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A reading of 118/76 mmHg falls in the normal category. Pulse pressure is 42 mmHg and estimated mean arterial pressure is 90 mmHg. Try the same figures in the [Blood Pressure Calculator](/blood-pressure-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Systolic pressure (top number): 118 mmHg, Diastolic pressure (bottom number): 76 mmHg), the [Blood Pressure Calculator](/blood-pressure-calculator) returns Reading category: Normal, Blood pressure: 118 / 76 mmHg, Pulse pressure: 42 mmHg, Estimated mean arterial pressure: 90 mmHg. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## One reading is not a diagnosis

Stress, pain, caffeine, exercise, posture, cuff size and measurement technique can all change a result. Home monitoring is most useful when readings are taken consistently and recorded over time. Categories use the higher-risk side when systolic and diastolic values fall into different bands, rather than averaging the two.

## When not to rely on a calculator

A reading of 180/120 mmHg or higher needs prompt professional assessment, especially if repeated after a short rest. Seek emergency help for severely high pressure accompanied by chest pain, breathlessness, weakness, vision change, confusion or other acute symptoms. Low pressure with fainting, confusion or severe weakness also needs urgent evaluation.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Measure at similar times and keep a dated log rather than relying on memory.
- Avoid caffeine, smoking and vigorous exercise for at least 30 minutes before a routine reading.
- Do not start, stop or adjust medication from a calculator result.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is normal blood pressure for adults?

Under common US categories, normal is below 120 systolic and below 80 diastolic. Other guidelines use different diagnostic thresholds, and individual clinical context matters. Try it with your own numbers in the [Blood Pressure Calculator](/blood-pressure-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Which number matters more?

Both matter. Classification uses the higher category indicated by either number; one should not be ignored simply because the other is normal. Try it with your own numbers in the [Blood Pressure Calculator](/blood-pressure-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can this diagnose hypertension?

No. Diagnosis uses repeated measurements and professional assessment. This tool classifies only the single reading you enter. Try it with your own numbers in the [Blood Pressure Calculator](/blood-pressure-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Blood Pressure Calculator use?
